sprint: Sprint 10 — Australia Residential Property Intelligence V2: NSW Reconciliation, Victoria Expansion, Cross-State Comparison and Automated Refresh
executive_summary: NSW's Sprint 9 dwelling-classification drift (18,712 records) was fully reconciled and independently verified. A documented state-adapter architecture and canonical data contracts now govern both states. Victoria's residential sales (VPSR, suburb grain) and rental market (Homes Victoria, dual suburb/LGA grain) were sourced, geography-mapped (95% suburb-match rate for sales via direct + one documented alias rule, zero fuzzy matching), built into local stores, and promoted to the branch (741 suburb snapshot rows, 18,507 sales/rent/yield timeseries rows). Victoria's supply/demographics/affordability data was confirmed already-national from prior sprints, needing no re-ingestion. A shared multi-state schema (jurisdiction column, not per-state duplicate tables), a 16-metric national canonical registry, and a security-tested cross-state comparison API (4 new SECURITY DEFINER interfaces) were delivered. A new internal explore/compare UI and a data-freshness observability page were built and browser-tested against real branch data. A refresh orchestration framework (dry-run by default, production-target hard-refused, proven live) closes out the automation requirement without enabling any schedule. All 16 phases completed. Production was never touched; the Supabase branch was never merged; no raw data files were committed; no paid infrastructure was increased.

recommended_next_step: Request explicit human approval before any Supabase branch merge or production deployment — this sprint deliberately stopped short of both, per the sprint's non-negotiable safety rules. Before that approval is sought, recommended follow-up (not urgent, not blocking): (1) re-verify NSW's gross_yield methodology against its own yield_sale_period_used/yield_rent_period_used columns specifically (this sprint's national_metric_validation_report only spot-checked VIC's formula exactly; NSW's was verified by design reasoning, not a fresh live recompute); (2) consider whether the ~50% VIC rent locality coverage gap (79 of 158 suburb-grain localities) is acceptable for launch or whether a documented LGA-only VIC rent experience should be the default until a further ASGS correspondence effort resolves more of Homes Victoria's custom groupings; (3) decide whether to invest in chart visualisation (recharts is installed, currently unused — Phase 12 explicitly deferred this).
